note: Habitually careless about cleanliness or neatness, especially in dress and appearance.
Educe means to draw out something latent or to cause it to emerge. It comes from Latin educere, to lead out.
Gainsay means to deny, contradict, or speak against something. Gainsaid is its past participle.

short: A Christian image of redemption through Christ.
note: In Revelation, the Lamb represents Christ: his blood redeems people and washes the robes of the faithful. The image also became prominent in Christian hymns.

short: Thomas Moore’s song of a warrior and his harp.
note: “The Minstrel Boy,” from Thomas Moore’s Irish Melodies, portrays a young harpist who fights for his country. Its second stanza links the silencing of his harp with resistance to slavery.

short: A traditional American song of longing and departure.
note: “Shenandoah” is a traditional American song with many variants, associated with river travel and sailors’ work songs. Its words commonly mention a beloved daughter and departure across the Missouri.

short: A song from Thomas Moore’s Irish Melodies.
note: Thomas Moore’s “My Gentle Harp” addresses a neglected instrument in sorrow, returning to it after disappointed hopes of freedom and peace. It belongs to his Irish Melodies.

short: To shift or slide a short distance.
note: An informal verb meaning to move a little way, especially by sliding or shuffling one’s body.

short: Flat metal strips used in vehicle suspension.
note: A leaf spring consists of a flexible metal strip or a stack of strips fastened together to support a vehicle and absorb road shocks.
Ravel can mean to undo a knitted or woven fabric into separate threads; it can also mean to entangle those threads.

short: An adjustable wind deflector mounted on a truck’s roof.
note: Varashield is a proprietary truck-mounted shield that redirects airflow to improve the vehicle’s aerodynamics. Its angle can be adjusted to suit the trailer’s height.
